Subject: Deployment mode evaluation: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — pricing & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and the recommended next steps so we can model costs for the two scenarios you asked about (pilot + production ramp):

Recap:
- Primary goals: low 99th-pct latency for customer-facing chat, predictable monthly cost for budgeting, and data isolation for regulated workflows.
- Workload profile: ~200M tokens/month estimated at steady state, spiky daytime traffic (50% of daily volume in a 6-hour window).
- Candidate deployment modes we discussed: Hosted API (fast to launch), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity for predictable throughput), Private (VPC/on-prem) for data isolation and compliance.

What I attached: deployment-cost-model.xlsx — contains two tabs: 1) Hosted per-token projection by month; 2) Dedicated reserved capacity vs burst economics; plus assumptions. Also included a draft SOW (ACME_SOW_draft.pdf) for an initial 3-month pilot.

High-level guidance (please see the attached model for line-item math):
- Hosted API: per-token pricing (prompt+completion). Good for pilots and variable volume. Example: at 200M tokens/month our baseline hosted estimate is ~ $120k–$160k/month depending on prompt/completion split and model family. No infra commitments, quick start.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): best for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. Typical savings vs hosted per-token are in the 30–50% range once you commit to a monthly pool. For your profile, a reserved pool sized for 200M tokens/month looks roughly like ~$60k–$90k/month in committed capacity, plus modest overage/burst if needed.
- Private VPC/On-prem: higher up-front and operating overhead (networking, KMS, monitoring), recommended if you require customer-managed networking or strict on-prem security. Unit economics can be similar to Dedicated at scale but procurement lead times are longer.

Questions for you to confirm (these drive the model assumptions):
1) Can you confirm the 200M tokens/month estimate and expected ramp timeline (months to steady state)?
2) What’s the baseline latency SLO you need (p95/p99 target)? That affects whether we recommend higher-tier GPUs or more aggressive batching.
3) Any hard constraints on data residency or private networking?

Next steps:
- If you confirm the three items above, I’ll update the cost model with your ramp and actual prompt lengths and send a side-by-side Hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison (hourly/weekly/monthly).
- If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute follow-up next week to walk through the model and pick a pilot configuration. Suggested times: Tue 8/3 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 8/4 13:00–14:00 PT.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the clarified inputs.

Regards,
Aditya Rao

Thanks Katie — great context. Short answers and details below so your procurement team can review ahead of the call.

Commitment terms (Dedicated):
- We offer both monthly and annual reserved commits. Monthly reserved pools are available with a 3-month minimum for Dedicated commitments (pilot-friendly); annual gives an additional discount (typically an extra 10–20% off monthly list).
- Commit sizing is in compute-pool units (concurrency/throughput) rather than strict token buckets; we map your traffic profile to a recommended pool size in the attached workbook.

Overages and bursting:
- Bursts beyond the reserved pool are allowed via a paid burst tier. Billing model options: a) per-token overage at a pre-negotiated overage rate (usually slightly higher than committed unit economics) or b) automatic burst credits where you pay a fixed burst reserve on top of commit. We typically model conservative bursts at 10–20% of monthly volume in the cost worksheet.

Private/VPC for pilot:
- For the pilot, we can deploy Redwood Dedicated into your AWS VPC using our private Dedicated offering (customer VPC peering + private connectors). That gives the isolation you asked for without a full on-prem install. Private/On-prem is still an option if you need air-gapped infrastructure, but lead times are longer.

Ballpark numbers (please treat these as directional until we add your precise prompt/completion mix):
- Hosted API (no commit): $0.0006–$0.0009 per token aggregated -> 200M tokens ≈ $120k–$180k/month.
- Dedicated (monthly reserved, 3-month min): committed pool for your profile ≈ $65k–$85k/month (saves ~40–55% vs hosted at identical throughput). Bursts billed separately per-token or via pre-purchased burst credits.
- Private/VPC (dedicated in your VPC): similar committed cost to Dedicated plus integration/setup fee (one-time) and potential networking/KMS costs.

I updated the deployment-cost-model.xlsx with an example 6-month ramp to 400M tokens and included separate sheets that show blended per-token equivalent and monthly cashflow for Hosted vs Dedicated. Please review the "Assumptions" sheet and let me know if we should swap any numbers.

Confirming the follow-up: Tue 8/3 10:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite. For procurement review, I’m copying Marissa (pricing lead) and Neha (contracts) on this thread so they can join the call or review the model ahead of time.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
